title: Kazakhstan — Cave Mosques, Chalk Canyons and the Steppe Road to Nauryz
subtitle: Four days in a 4x4 across Mangystau, then Silk Road ruins and a night train to the spring festival
summary: A fourteen-day Kazakhstan-only route: Astana, four days of tent camping across the Mangystau desert (chalk cliffs, concretions, underground mosques), the Sufi and Silk Road sites around Turkistan, an overnight train east, and Nauryz in Almaty with a Bronze Age petroglyph day.
introduction: Fly into the steppe capital Astana, then south-west to Aktau on the Caspian and spend four days in a 4x4 across Mangystau: concretions at Torysh, the white and ochre rim of the Ustyurt plateau at Bozzhyra, and mosques cut into the rock at Shakpak-Ata and Beket-Ata, all under cold clear March skies and with tents at night. Next, the south: Otrar's Silk Road ruins, the Yasawi mausoleum in Turkistan and the earthen walls of Sauran. A sleeper train carries you 1,300 km to Almaty for Nauryz on 21 March, the Kazakh spring new year.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a self-drive loop through a well-served country; here the dry desert driving is done by a local 4x4 driver, camping is in a landscape with almost no other visitors, and the culture is Sufi and nomadic rather than Gulf. The second half adds a night train and a national festival that Oman cannot offer.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Standard Kazakhstan packages cover Almaty, Charyn and Astana in comfort. This route skips the Almaty mountains and spends most of its days in Mangystau and the Turkistan region, which see few foreign winter visitors, and uses a sleeper train instead of internal flights.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: The Central Asia route (D21) combines Uzbekistan's tiled cities with a short Almaty finish. This route is Kazakhstan only, centred on Caspian desert, cave mosques and Sufi pilgrimage, and shares only the arrival city's airport with it.

coordinates.label: Turkistan, southern Kazakhstan (route centre of gravity)

duration.note: Day 1 outbound (arrive late), day 14 return. Dates assumed 9-22 March 2027 so that day 13 is 21 March, Nauryz.

recommendedTravelWindow.window: About 9-22 March 2027, ending on Nauryz (21 March)
recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: March is above freezing by day in the south and on the Caspian coast, nights in Mangystau hover around 0 C rather than -10 C, and Nauryz falls on 21 March. February is feasible but much colder: Astana nights near -20 C and Mangystau tent nights well below freezing.

februarySuitability.summary: Cold: Astana days about -12 to -5 C, Mangystau nights around -8 C. Camping is possible with proper kit but harsh, and snow can close tracks; no Nauryz festival.

marchSuitability.summary: Cold but workable: Mangystau days 8-12 C and nights 0-3 C, southern Kazakhstan 10-15 C by day, Almaty 5-12 C. Ramadan ends 9 March; Nauryz holiday on 21-23 March.

climate.regionNote: Continental desert and steppe climate; Astana is among the coldest capital cities in the world. Values are climate normals across the route, not a forecast; ranges cover Astana (coldest) to Turkistan and Shymkent (mildest).

february.rainfall: Low; snow possible in Astana and Almaty
february.notes: Astana -15 C at night; Mangystau days near 0-5 C with strong wind.

march.rainfall: Low to moderate; rain or wet snow possible
march.notes: Mangystau days 8-11 C and nights 0-3 C; Turkistan 10-15 C; Almaty 5-12 C; strong winds on the Ustyurt rim.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Mangystau tracks usually remain open in March but can be muddy or snow-covered after storms; Almaty mountain skiing is not part of this route. Tamgaly is reached by tarmac.
climate.seaConditions: Caspian shore is cold (about 3-6 C) and not used for swimming.
climate.airQuality: Astana winter heating produces some haze; desert and steppe sections are clear.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Spring migration of birds on the Caspian coast starts in March; wild sheep (argali relatives) and gazelles are possible on the Ustyurt plateau but not guaranteed.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Nauryz
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: 21-23 March 2027 (Sunday to Tuesday); possible replacement day off on 24 March
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Festival with yurt towns, food, music and games in cities; transport and hotels are busy and prices rise; book return flights and trains early. Programme for 2027 not yet published.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Moon-sighting dependent; Kazakhstan is secular and Oraza Ait is not the main national holiday, so little disruption.

climate.ramadan2027: Expected about 8 February to 9 March 2027; the trip starts on its last day. Kazakhstan is a secular country and most restaurants stay open, so impact is minimal; some pilgrimage sites may be busier around Eid.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Lunar New Year (6 February 2027) is not observed in Kazakhstan.
climate.tourismDemand: Low in March: Mangystau and Turkistan see few foreign visitors outside May-June and September; Nauryz is a domestic peak in Almaty and hotels there fill.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Paris-Astana and Almaty fares are generally lower in late winter than in summer, but Nauryz weekend pushes domestic fares and the Almaty return up; book 8-10 weeks ahead.

geography.summary: From the Caspian desert and the Ustyurt plateau in the west through the Syr Darya plain in the south to the foothills of the Tian Shan in the south-east, with steppe in between.
geography.distinctive: Kazakhstan's lowest point (Karagiye, -132 m), concretion fields and chalk badlands within a day's 4x4 drive of one another, without the mountain skiing and lake scenery of the neighbouring Central Asia route.

culture.summary: Sufi pilgrimage in Mangystau and Turkistan, Silk Road archaeology, Bronze Age rock art and the Kazakh spring festival, set against Soviet and post-Soviet cities.

culturalHighlights.name: Beket-Ata and Shakpak-Ata
culturalHighlights.description: Pilgrimage sites of the Sufi tradition in Mangyshlak, visited as guests with the local caretaker.

culturalHighlights.name: Khoja Ahmed Yasawi mausoleum
culturalHighlights.description: Begun by Timur in 1389 and never finished; Yasawi is the founder of the Turkic Sufi tradition.

culturalHighlights.name: Otrar and Sauran
culturalHighlights.description: Medieval trading cities of the Syr Darya, from Genghis Khan's siege to the Kazakh Khanate.

culturalHighlights.name: Nauryz
culturalHighlights.description: Yurts, shared food, music and games on 21 March; the group joins public events as guests.

adventureHighlights.name: Four days of 4x4 and tent camping in Mangystau
adventureHighlights.description: Off-road driving by a local driver; nights near freezing and strong wind.

adventureHighlights.name: Canyon hikes at Bozzhyra and Beket-Ata
adventureHighlights.description: Easy to moderate walks of 3-4 hours on rough ground.

adventureHighlights.name: 1,300 km overnight train
adventureHighlights.description: Turkistan to Almaty in a sleeper berth, a rail leg of 15-20 hours.

signatureExperiences.title: Four-day tent camp across Mangystau
signatureExperiences.description: Aktau to Shakpak-Ata, Torysh, Sherkala, Bozzhyra and Beket-Ata, with three tent nights.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Chalk cliffs, concretions and cave mosques with almost no other visitors in March.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a private 4x4 with driver for four days (about EUR 400/day in 2027 for up to 4 people), including tents, sleeping bags and full board; confirm March operation and sleeping bags rated to -5 C.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Per person for four days with four people sharing one car.

signatureExperiences.title: Beket-Ata underground mosque
signatureExperiences.description: A walk of 1.5 km into the canyon to a mosque cut into the rock and a pilgrimage place for western Kazakhstan.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A living pilgrimage site, quiet in March.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Visit with the 4x4 driver and local caretaker; dress modestly.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Included in the 4x4 package; donation customary.

signatureExperiences.title: Yasawi mausoleum and the Sufi south
signatureExperiences.description: Otrar, Arystan Bab, the Yasawi mausoleum and Sauran across two days.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A UNESCO mausoleum begun by Timur plus empty Silk Road cities.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Hired car with driver for Otrar and Sauran (about EUR 90-110 per day), walking in Turkistan.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Driver days for four, plus entrance fees.

signatureExperiences.title: Overnight sleeper train and Nauryz
signatureExperiences.description: A sleeper from Turkistan to Almaty, then Nauryz in the city.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Crosses 1,300 km of steppe on a train used by locals and ends on the national spring festival.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Buy tickets as early as possible (about 60 days ahead in many cases) and confirm Nauryz week seats.

travelStyle.summary: Guided 4x4 camping in Mangystau, hired drivers and trains elsewhere; no self-drive.

transport.summary: Flights Astana-Aktau and Aktau-Shymkent, a driven 4x4 in Mangystau, hired cars with drivers in the south, a sleeper train to Almaty.

modes.description: FlyArystan, SCAT and Air Astana; about EUR 70-100 per segment.
One vehicle for four people with camping gear; about EUR 400 per day in the 2027 season.
Day hire in the south and for Tamgaly, about EUR 90-140.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental is not recommended in Mangystau; operators supply driver-guided 4x4s. In towns, taxis are cheap; use ordered rides only.

drivingRequirements.summary: Driven transport only: winter conditions on unmarked tracks, scarce fuel and a 4x4 requirement make self-drive unwise, and Mangystau operators supply drivers.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: A 1968 International Driving Permit is required with some licences (UK FCDO); not needed when driven by a local.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences; not needed in this plan.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycles or scooters; none of the plan requires them.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hired 4x4 driver in Mangystau, hired cars with driver for day trips, trains and domestic flights elsewhere.

accommodation.summary: Hotels in cities, tents in Mangystau, a guesthouse or yurt option at Beket-Ata or Bozzhyra, and a train berth.
types: Guesthouse or yurt (about EUR 20 per person)

camping.summary: Wild camping in Mangystau with operator tents and sleeping bags; nights near freezing and windy, so a warm bag and liners are required. Guesthouse alternatives are available.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Moderate: long 4x4 days of 4-6 hours, cold nights, canyon hikes of 3-4 hours at low altitude, an overnight train and 1,900 km flights.

itinerary.summary: Astana, flight to Aktau, four days of 4x4 camping across Mangystau, flight to Shymkent, Otrar-Turkistan-Sauran, a night train to Almaty, Tamgaly and Nauryz, flight home.

stops.name: Astana Airport (NQZ)
stops.description: Arrival airport of the open-jaw journey; the ETA is mandatory here from 1 January 2027.
stops.geography: Steppe capital at about 350 m, cold in March.
stops.transport: Taxi or airport bus; Astana-Aktau flight on day 3.

stops.name: Astana: Baiterek and Hazret Sultan
stops.description: The capital built since 1997: Baiterek tower, the Hazret Sultan mosque and the governmental axis, seen on one cold day to set the Kazakh state against the nomad landscapes that follow.
activities: Khan Shatyr indoor tropical park for warmth
stops.culturalImportance: Capital since 1997; a showcase of post-Soviet statecraft and Eurasian architecture.
stops.geography: Flat steppe on the Ishim river.

stops.name: Aktau, Caspian shore
stops.description: Soviet-planned Caspian port without street names, the base for supplies, the driver meeting and the end of the Mangystau loop.
stops.culturalImportance: A planned industrial town founded in the early Soviet 1960s; now the hub of Mangystau.
stops.geography: Desert shore of the Caspian, mean March day about 8-11 C.
stops.transport: Taxi; Astana flights; Shymkent flight on day 8.

stops.name: Shakpak-Ata underground mosque
stops.description: A small mosque cut into a limestone cliff above the Caspian steppe,; one of the underground mosques of the Mangyshlak peninsula.
activities: Photograph exterior only unless the caretaker agrees
stops.culturalImportance: Local pilgrimage place of the Sufi tradition of the peninsula.

stops.name: Torysh valley of balls
stops.description: A field of rounded sandstone concretions, some a metre or more across, eroding out of a clay slope.
activities: Walk among concretions at low sun
stops.geography: Cretaceous-Paleogene sediments of the Mangyshlak peninsula.

stops.name: Mount Sherkala
stops.description: A lone lion-shaped hill on the steppe, the first night in a tent camp with stars and no light.
activities: Evening climb or walk around the hill
stops.culturalImportance: Local legend site; Sherkala means lion fortress.
stops.geography: Isolated hill rising from flat steppe.
stops.accommodation: Tents, sleeping bags and mats from the operator.

stops.name: Karagiye Depression
stops.description: The lowest point in Kazakhstan, 132 m below sea level, a stark salt-and-clay basin on the way east.

stops.name: Bozzhyra tract
stops.description: White, ochre and pink pinnacles on the western rim of the Ustyurt plateau, the best-known landscape of Mangystau, camped on and hiked on two days.
stops.culturalImportance: Ustyurt plateau shared with Uzbekistan; nomadic grazing land.
stops.geography: Chalk-and-clay cliffs; the tract is not part of the Ustyurt Nature Reserve.
stops.transport: 4x4 on 270-300 km of mixed asphalt and track from Aktau.
stops.accommodation: Tents; yurt or guesthouse on request (about EUR 20 per person).

stops.name: Beket-Ata underground mosque
stops.description: The most important pilgrimage site of western Kazakhstan, an underground mosque entered after a walk of about 1.5 km into the canyon.
stops.culturalImportance: Burial place of the 18th-century Sufi teacher Beket-Ata.
stops.geography: Canyon on the Ustyurt plateau edge.
stops.accommodation: Tent camp or small local guesthouse.

stops.name: Shymkent
stops.description: Southern Kazakhstan's biggest city by the Uzbek border, a bazaar and plov base before Otrar.
stops.geography: Foothills of the western Tian Shan.
stops.transport: Flight from Aktau (confirm routing), then driver.

stops.name: Otrar archaeological site
stops.description: The ruined Silk Road city whose governor provoked Genghis Khan's invasion in 1218-1219, on the Syr Darya plain.
stops.culturalImportance: Birthplace of the philosopher al-Farabi and death place of Timur (1405).

stops.name: Arystan Bab mausoleum
stops.description: The mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi's teacher, a living pilgrimage place near Otrar.
stops.culturalImportance: Teacher and spiritual guide of Yasawi; important Sufi site.

stops.name: Turkistan: Khoja Ahmed Yasawi mausoleum
stops.description: The Timurid mausoleum of the Sufi poet Yasawi, UNESCO-listed in 2003, with the largest brick dome in Central Asia, in a town rebuilt as a pilgrimage and tourism centre.
stops.culturalImportance: Spiritual capital of the Turkic world; Kazakh khans were buried here.

stops.name: Sauran ruins
stops.description: A walled medieval city on the steppe north-west of Turkistan, a Kazakh Khanate city before the court moved to Turkistan.
stops.transport: Hired car about 45 km each way.

stops.name: Almaty (Kok-Tobe and city)
stops.description: The former capital below the Trans-Ili Alatau, used here only for arrival by night train, Nauryz and the flight home; its mountain winter sports are left to the Central Asia route.
stops.transport: Night train from Turkistan; taxi and metro.

stops.name: Tamgaly petroglyphs
stops.description: A UNESCO-listed Bronze Age sanctuary with thousands of carvings, about 170 km north-west of Almaty.
stops.culturalImportance: About 5,000 petroglyphs on 48 sites, Bronze Age to the 19th century.
stops.geography: Dry hills of the Chu-Ili range.

budget.exceptionalJustification: The realistic total is about EUR 2,310 per person, above the preferred EUR 2,000, because roughly a third is the one-stop open-jaw flight (EUR 750) and about EUR 400 per person is the four-day private 4x4 with camping gear and full board, the only practical way to reach Bozzhyra and the underground mosques in March. The economical variant (about EUR 1,610) uses the early-booking 4x4 rate, guesthouses and cheaper flights and stays inside the preferred band.

scenarioNotes.economical: Early-booking 4x4 rate of EUR 350 a day, hostels and guesthouses, third-class sleeper, no English guide and cheapest flights.
scenarioNotes.realistic: EUR 400 a day 4x4 with camping and full board, mid-range twin rooms, one-stop open-jaw flights, three hired-car days and an English guide on five days.
scenarioNotes.comfortable: Five days of 4x4, upper-range hotels, compartment sleeper, guides on seven days and flexible fares.

security.summary: No official advisory reviewed advises against all or all-but-essential travel on the assessed route; the only formally discouraged area, the Semipalatinsk test zone, and the permit-only Baikonur and Kyzylorda areas are avoided. Terrorism risk is low but not zero.
security.assessedRoute: Astana, Aktau and Mangystau (Shakpak-Ata, Torysh, Sherkala, Karagiye, Bozzhyra, Beket-Ata), Shymkent, Otrar and Turkistan, Sauran, the overnight train to Almaty, Tamgaly and Almaty. Excludes Semipalatinsk and Kurchatov, Baikonur and the Karmakchi and Kazalinsk districts, Gvardeyskiy, and restricted border strips.

advisories.level: Zone south of Kurchatov and Semipalatinsk formally advised against; rest of country reinforced vigilance. Page updated 22 and 19 October 2026; zone map 10 March 2026.

advisories.routeImpact: Route does not enter either area.

advisories.level: Visa exemption for French citizens, generally 30 days; ETA mandatory at Aktau airport from 1 Nov 2026 and at Astana and Almaty airports from 1 Jan 2027.
advisories.routeImpact: Apply for ETA at least 72 h before arrival.

advisories.level: No area listed as against-all or all-but-essential travel in the pages read; updated 30 October 2026. Closed areas needing permission: Gvardeyskiy, Baikonur, Karmakchi and Kazalinsk districts.
advisories.routeImpact: Route does not enter closed areas.

advisories.level: Yellow (particular security risks), updated 18 November 2026; demonstrations can turn violent in Almaty and large cities.
advisories.routeImpact: Avoid demonstrations; Nauryz events are public holidays but not protests.

kidnappingRisk.note: No kidnapping warnings in the reviewed advice.

security.medicalAccess: Good in Astana, Almaty and Aktau; limited outside big cities, and patients may need evacuation abroad.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Take travel insurance covering camping, hiking and off-road 4x4 trips, plus medical repatriation; check exclusions for restricted zones.
security.reassessmentRequired: Recheck French, UK and Dutch advisories before booking and before departure; verify ETA rules, the Aktau-Shymkent flight and winter track conditions.

practicalRequirements.visa: Visa-free entry for French citizens for up to 30 days; UK page also gives 30 days; the ETA is free and valid for 180 days.
practicalRequirements.entry: Apply for ETA at least 72 hours before arrival (mandatory at Astana and Almaty airports from 1 January 2027; strictly required from 1 July 2027); hotel registers arrival within 3 working days.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 30 days after arrival per UK advice; French page does not state a figure; the Dutch page says six months, so keep six months to be safe.
permits: No permit for the planned route; Baikonur and restricted border zones need approval about ten days ahead and are not planned
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Local SIM cards are cheap with Wi-Fi in cities; coverage in Mangystau is patchy.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards in cities; carry tenge cash for villages, guesthouses and bazaars; ATMs in Aktau.
practicalRequirements.medical: Carry a first-aid kit; limited facilities outside cities; measles alert for 2026.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Fuel is included in the 4x4 package; stations are scarce outside cities.
equipment: Sleeping-bag liner and warm clothing for -5 to 5 C nights

advantages: Mangystau's landscapes with very few visitors in March
UNESCO and Sufi heritage in Turkistan
Visa-free for French citizens and low travel cost on the ground
Ends with the Nauryz national festival
Distinct from the Central Asia route: no Almaty skiing or Charyn
disadvantages: Cold camping nights and strong wind
Large distances: about 1,900 km flights each way and a 15-20 h train
uncertainties: Whether Mangystau 4x4 operators run in March and at what price
Direct Aktau-Shymkent flight or a connection
Nauryz 2027 programme and the exact days off

sources.title: Kazakhstan - Conseils aux voyageurs (France Diplomatie)
sources.publisher: France Diplomatie (Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères)
claims: Page updated 22 October 2026; French citizens visa-exempt for stays generally up to 30 days

Electronic Entry Authorisation (ETA, QazETA): mandatory at Aktau airport from 1 Nov 2026, at Astana and Almaty airports from 1 Jan 2027, all crossings from 1 Mar 2027, strictly required from 1 Jul 2027; free, 72 h before arrival, valid 180 days
General alerts: reinforced vigilance for French nationals abroad (10 Sep 2026) and measles (13 Mar 2026)

sources.title: Kazakhstan - Sécurité (France Diplomatie)
sources.publisher: France Diplomatie (Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères)
claims: Only the zone south of Kurchatov and Semipalatinsk (Soviet nuclear test radioactivity) is formally advised against; the rest of the country is in reinforced-vigilance zone
Restricted zones, including parts of Baikonur, require prior authorisation (about ten days from immigration police)
Terrorist threat towards French nationals considered low but cannot be ruled out. Page updated 19 October 2026; zone map 10 March 2026

sources.title: Foreign travel advice Kazakhstan (UK FCDO)
claims: Last updated 30 October 2026; advice still current on 28 Nov 2026
No area listed as against-all or all-but-essential travel in the pages read
Update concerned the Electronic Travel Authorisation

sources.title: Kazakhstan: Safety and security (UK FCDO)
claims: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out; unauthorised protests lead to arrest
Closed areas needing permission: Gvardeyskiy (Almaty region), Baikonur, Karmakchi and Kazalinsk districts (Kyzylorda region)
Road safety: poorly maintained cars, unmarked roadworks, stray animals, scarce fuel stations outside cities, 1968 IDP required with a UK licence; snow and ice can block roads in winter
Photography restricted near military sites, borders and airports; drones need a licence

sources.title: Kazakhstan: Entry requirements (UK FCDO)
claims: Visa-free stays of up to 30 days for tourism (UK-citizen page; the French page states the same 30 days for French citizens)
Hotel or host must register arrival within 3 working days
ETA free, valid 180 days, apply at least 72 hours ahead; mandatory and enforced from 1 July 2027

sources.title: Reisadvies Kazachstan (Nederland Wereldwijd)
claims: Yellow level (particular security risks) for the whole country, updated 18 November 2026
Demonstrations in Almaty and large cities can turn violent; severe earthquakes possible in the south-east; limited medical facilities outside big cities
Photography of military objects, government buildings and officials is prohibited; drugs and vapes strictly prohibited

sources.title: Kazakhstan Travel Advisory (US Department of State)
claims: Level 1 (exercise normal precautions), date issued 18 August 2026, as reported by news summaries; the State Department page itself returned HTTP 403 to our fetch, so the level was not read first-hand
Notes limited medical care, flooding and financial scams

sources.title: Universal Mangystau private 4x4 tours (Eurasia Travel)

Includes experienced driver, full camping equipment (tents, mats, sleeping bags, tables, chairs), full board on multi-day trips and water; English guide about EUR 60/day extra, guesthouse/yurt night about EUR 20 per person on request
5-day itinerary Jygylgan, Qapamsay, Torysh, Bozjyra, Tuzbaiyr, Karagiye; seasonal note 'Autumn - Spring best'; winter/March operation not stated

sources.title: Mangystau classic tour, 5 days (Advantour)
claims: Private 5-day classic tour listed from US$690 per person; 3-day express (Torysh, Bozzhyra, Kyzylkup) from US$575
4x4 transfers with maximum 3 passengers; tent camping may be replaced by guesthouses in severe weather at extra cost

sources.title: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi (Wikipedia)
claims: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003; construction began 1389 under Timur and stopped at his death in 1405
Largest extant brick dome in Central Asia (about 18.2 m diameter); coordinates 43.2978 N, 68.2708 E

sources.title: Otrar (Wikipedia)
claims: Silk Road city of the Turkistan Region, about 120 km north-west of Shymkent and 50 km from Turkistan
Genghis Khan besieged Otrar in 1219 after the governor executed a Mongol caravan; Timur died there in February 1405

sources.title: Tamgaly (Wikipedia)
claims: About 5,000 petroglyphs on 48 sites, Bronze Age to the 18th-19th century; UNESCO inscription 2004
About 170 km north-west of Almaty, coordinates 43.8033 N, 75.535 E

sources.title: Mangystau Region (Wikipedia)
claims: Continental climate with cold winters; January mean about -3 C; annual rainfall about 150 mm
Karagiye depression bottom is 132 m below sea level; Torysh is the 'Valley of Balls' of rounded concretions

claims: Search-result snapshot lists Paris-Astana fares from about EUR 758 (undated fare snapshot, so treated as representative, not a live quote)
Skyscanner snapshot (March 2026) lists no non-stop Astana-Paris flights, so one stop (Istanbul or another hub) is assumed

sources.title: Astana to Aktau flights (Expedia / Trip.com fare pages)

sources.title: Holidays and Observances in Kazakhstan in 2027 (timeanddate)
claims: Nauryz public holiday 21-23 March 2027 (Sunday to Tuesday); a replacement day off on Wednesday 24 March is listed but the exact transfer depends on a Cabinet decision
